function.description: Calculate the future value of an investment given the principal, interest rate and term. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

principal.description: The initial amount of the investment. This is a float type value.

interest_rate.description: The annual interest rate in percentage. Enter as a decimal (for 5%, enter 0.05). This is a float type value.

term.description: The term of the investment in years.

compounding.description: The number of times that interest is compounded per year. Default is 1 (annually).

message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic chills, modern scares, and hidden gems—so whether you’re looking for something new or revisiting old favorites, there should be plenty on this list:

| # | Title & Year | Why It Stands Out |
|---|--------------|--------------------|
| **1** | *The Shining* (1980) – Stanley Kubrick adaptation of Stephen King’s novel | Iconic atmosphere, unsettling score, Jack Nicholson’s unforgettable performance. |
| **2** | *Hereditary* (2018) – Ari Aster’s psychological‑family‑torture masterpiece | Deep dread built from family trauma; truly unnerving visuals. |
| **3** | *Get Out* (2017) – Jordan Peele’s social satire meets jump‑scares | Clever blend of horror + sharp cultural critique. |
| **4** | *Midsommar* (2019) – Another Ari Aster film but set in daylight | Contrasts bright Swedish summer with horrific cult rituals. |
| **5** | *A Quiet Place* (2018) – John Krasinski’s tense silence thriller | Unique premise where sound equals death; strong emotional core. |
| **6** | *It Follows* (2014) – Creepy supernatural curse delivered via slow‑moving entity | Distinctive “infinite” threat concept; retro synth soundtrack. |
| **7** | *Suspiria* (1977) – Dario Argento’s color‑splashed giallo | Classic Italian horror with striking visual style. |
| **8** | *Pan's Labyrinth* (2006) – Guillermo del Toro’s dark fairy tale | Beautifully crafted fantasy world mixed with brutal reality. |
| **9** | *The Babadook* (2014) – Australian indie about grief turned monster | Psychological depth plus effective creature design. |
| **10** | *Evil Dead II* (1987) – Sam Raimi’s over-the-top gore & humor | Cult favorite blending campy fun with genuine terror. |

### Bonus Picks if You Want Something Different

| # | Title & Year | What Makes It Special |
|---|--------------|-----------------------|
| **11** | *Creepshow* (1982) – anthology directed by George A. Romero | Short stories each with its own twist; great for quick thrills. |
| **12** | *The Witch* (2015) – Robert Eggers’ period‑period paranoia | Slow burn, authentic historical detail, eerie folk‑magic vibe. |
| **13** | *Train to Busan* (2016) – Korean zombie action | Fast pacing, heartfelt characters amid apocalyptic chaos. |
| **14** | *REC* (2007) – Spanish found‑footage infection outbreak | Realistic camera work creates intense claustrophobia. |
| **15** | *Coraline* (2009) – Stop‑motion animated nightmare | Visually stunning yet creepy story for all ages. |

Feel free to pick based on your mood—whether it’s atmospheric dread, body‑horror, or socially relevant themes—and enjoy the fright!
